en.t: The monitoring for the AI system I built runs in Power BI.
en.d: Not a specialized observability platform. A report, on a schedule, that a business owner already knows how to open without me in the room. People find that underwhelming until they see what is on it. It does not track model latency. It tracks how many outputs a validation rule blocked this week, which rule blocked them, and how long a human took to approve…

en.t: Three agents, and one rule none of them can break.
en.d: That is the shape of the retail intelligence pipeline I built this year, and the rule matters more than the agents do. Agent one acquires competitor data. Agent two enriches market signals on Delta Lake. Agent three generates pricing recommendations through RAG, combining those external signals with internal sales history. Each agent owns one job and hands…

en.t: We built a RAG system over a product catalogue.
en.d: Retrieval was the part that took the least time. The system indexes a company's product and inventory catalogue in a vector database, and LangChain orchestrates the Claude API to answer natural language questions grounded in their own data. Getting that working is a known problem now. There are tutorials. What took the time was everything the tutorials…

en.t: The most useful governance tool I have used on an AI project is a text file.
en.d: On a national data program I documented architecture decisions as ADRs. Architecture Decision Records. It is an old software engineering practice: one short document per significant decision, stating what we chose, what we rejected, and why. Dated, and never edited after the fact. We used it across a cross functional AI and data portfolio. Different teams,…

en.t: Before we wrote a single line of code, I recommended killing two of the workstreams.

My first real deliverable was a data readiness audit that said two pieces of it were not going to survive production. Not because the idea was wrong. en.d: Most data platform failures aren't modeling problems. They're governance problems that got discovered too late. I built a small lakehouse pipeline that puts the audit before the build instead of after, because the batch with a broken primary key or a silently renamed column doesn't fail loudly in development.
